Kimberly / Jonas — forwarding Novacorp's redlines and logo package. Key asks from them are the confidentiality carveout for earnings windows and an "asset escrow" requirement.

Quick context: this is a mid-size strategic pilot (DC-78321). Sales wants two things: (1) keep the publicity flow light so we can use Novacorp as a reference after launch and (2) not blow up the deal timeline with a protracted legal sprint.

My initial thoughts:
- We should propose a narrow publicity carveout that allows Novacorp to make regulatory/earnings disclosures, but otherwise keeps marketing announcements governed by a 14-day approval window.
- Escrow idea: accept temporary escrow of high-res logo files (hosted in our shared Drive with limited access) but reject a perpetual escrow that prevents us from preparing collateral in advance.

Can you draft a short redline that preserves our standard reference approval process but accommodates a 48–72 hour embargo exception for announced earnings? I've attached a quick starter redline (redline_response_MSAR_08142028.docx).

Thanks — Hannah

message_3:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 11:17:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Novacorp redlines — recommended language and risk notes

Hannah / Jonas — reviewed Novacorp's redlines and Hannah's suggested starter. High level: we can meet them most of the way with careful, narrow language. Key recommendations below (I'll incorporate into the attached redline):

1) Confidentiality carveout (earnings/regulatory):
- Proposed text: "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Customer may disclose the existence of the Agreement and the fact of Customer's relationship with Provider in regulatory filings or other legally compelled disclosures; Customer will provide Provider with commercially reasonable prior notice to the extent practicable."
- Rationale: gives them the ability to comply with securities/regulatory obligations without giving unlimited publicity rights.

2) Publicity and references (marketing case studies):
- Maintain our standard approval window of 14 calendar days for any marketing use (quotes, logos, case studies).
- Add an exception for a limited embargo period (48–72 hours) only where the announcement is tied to an earnings release; Customer must still provide final text and artwork for written approval not later than 3 business days prior to release when practicable.

3) Logo / asset escrow:
- Accept temporary escrow of master vector files in a controlled shared folder (Redwood-managed Drive folder with access logs). We will not accept requirements that restrict pre-production use; propose a clause: "Provider may hold and prepare Provider marketing materials using escrowed logo files, provided Provider does not publicly publish such materials until Customer's written approval or the agreed embargo expires."
- Require mutual right to audit access logs for the escrow folder once per quarter.

4) Approval timelines and remedies:
- If Customer does not respond within the 14-day window, approval is deemed granted. For earnings-related embargoes, if Customer misses the 48–72h window without notice, Provider may proceed after sending a final notice and waiting 24 hours.

5) Boilerplate tweaks: limit the publicity clause to non-confidential marketing materials to avoid inadvertent disclosure of trade secrets.

I'll attach the redline and a clean clause summary for exec sign-off. Two asks for Sales/legal:
- Jonas: confirm this is commercially acceptable (particularly the deemed-approval fallback).
- Hannah: if Sales is comfortable, I'll finalize and send a consolidated redline back to NovaCorp and propose a DocuSign envelope for an addendum.

Attachment: redline_response_MSAR_08142028.docx (docx)

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 16 Aug 2028 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novacorp redlines — press & logo usage / asset escrow proposal

Sarah — thanks for sending the redlines and logo package. We've reviewed and attached our consolidated response. Summary of the agreed items we are proposing:

- Confidentiality carveout for regulatory/earnings disclosures (narrow scope; notice to Redwood where practicable).
- Marketing/reference approval remains a 14-calendar-day window; deemed approval if no response in 14 days.
- Earnings-related announcement: limited embargo exception of up to 72 hours, with requirement that Novacorp provide final text/artwork as soon as available (ideally 3 business days prior).
- Logo escrow: Redwood will hold master logo assets in a limited-access Drive folder (access logs retained). Redwood may prepare collateral from those assets but will not publish until Customer approval or embargo expiry. Quarterly audit right for access logs.

We believe this keeps Novacorp's compliance needs intact while preserving our ability to prepare joint materials and avoid unnecessary delays to launch. If this aligns with your expectations, can you: (a) confirm by EOD Monday, Aug 19, or (b) propose final edits and we'll route to DocuSign?

I've attached the consolidated redline and a short clean clause summary for your legal team. If accepted, I'll send a DocuSign envelope for the addendum and the signature page.

Attachments: redline_response_MSAR_08142028.docx (docx), signature_page_novacorp.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Sales Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
